A view becomes [bit_len << 4][first byte][BinRef], so a binary's length sits at one place for both forms. A match reads its subject's length once and makes no kind test for a cursor. GC agreed the layout: its fz-9x7.11 steps C1-C6 never assume view word 0 is a pointer, and the forwarding.rs doc is to be updated. Census: /Users/j5n/Workspace/fz-binaries/view-layout.md (all view word access is in bits.rs; two compiler loads in prim.rs; the collector's marker rule already holds). Spike: the whole suite passes; the match loop goes from 33.6 to 19.4 instructions per iteration (BEAM 33.4). Builder: Binary Handling.

Agreed by Optimize and Binary Handling (2026-11-19): fz-nml.29.1 marks a view through one accessor and masks the mark in a view's word 0. Whoever builds this ticket replaces that accessor's body and deletes the view-word masking fz-nml.29.1 adds.
title: A binary view holds its length first
